items.current_truth: One owner answers how far a move reaches and what region it covers: `MoveSpec::frame_data()`. items.name: How far a hit launches its victim
items.current_truth: One owner answers how far a hit launches its victim: `ambition_entity_catalog::launch::launch_speed`. It used to be answered twice. `ambition_combat::util::scaled_knockback` resolved a hit as `base + growth x growth_base(base) x growth_scale x victim_damage / weight`, folded with rage; `ambition_entity_catalog::LaunchEnvelope::at` -- the function the fighter brain ranks its FINISHERS with -- evaluated `base + growth x victim_damage`, and its own doc argued the omission was safe because the remaining factors are "COMMON to every candidate one attacker weighs against one opponent, so none of them can reorder a kit". Each omitted factor multiplies the PERCENT TERM and not `base`, so it moves the CROSSOVER between two candidates: d* = (b2 - b1) * weight / (growth_scale * growth_base * (g1 - g2)). Measured 2026-09-20: George Booul's forward smash (185, 3.45) beats his up smash (178, 6.28) at 2 points of victim damage under the brain's copy (191.90 against 190.56) and loses to it under the smash stage's declared percent scale 1.25 against a 0.85-weight body (195.15 against 196.47). `scaled_knockback` and `rage_for_growth` are deleted and `GrowthBaseCurve` moved with the law; `ambition_combat` still RESOLVES every input through `ResolvedCombatTuning` and no longer owns the arithmetic they are spent on. The stage's half of the law reaches the brain through `WorldView::launch_law` and `PerceivedActor::knockback_weight`. SECOND DEFECT ON THE SAME AXIS, raised by review 2026-09-20 one commit after the collapse and repaired the same day: moving the arithmetic into one function did not make the two sides agree, because each still COLLAPSED `knockback_growth: Option<f32>` before calling it, and they collapsed it differently. `Some(g)` states a growth (`Some(0.0)` is the documented FIXED launch) and `None` means "the ruleset decides", resolving to `base * CombatRules::knockback_growth`; the hit resolver spent the fallback and `LaunchEnvelope::with_volume` spent `unwrap_or(0.0)`. Two shipped moves author `None` -- `cellular_pulse` (base 140) and `performer_trapdoor` (base 150) -- and the smash stage declares 0.02 with a percent scale of 1.25, so at 100% against the reference body the stage threw the pulse 490px/s while the brain priced it 140 and, reading it as a set launch, declined its rage as well. => The collapse now belongs to the law: `launch_speed` takes the `Option` and `LaunchConditions` carries `ruleset_growth`, so there is exactly one place where `None` becomes a number. `LaunchEnvelope` keeps the `Option` on its flat line and `grows()` became `grows_under(conditions)`, because the question has two answers -- a `None` volume is a set launch in an undeclared world and a percent-scaling one on a stage that declares a fallback.
